title: Psalms Chapter 116 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 116 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 116 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 116.

questions.question: In Psalms 116, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The sorrows of death compassed me
Then called I upon the name of the LORD
questions.explanation: The first statement in the chapter is 'I love the LORD' as stated in Psalms 116:1.

questions.question: Why does the psalmist love the LORD?
options: Because he hath inclined his ear unto me
Because he hath heard my voice and my supplications
questions.correctAnswer: Because he hath heard my voice and my supplications
questions.explanation: The psalmist loves the LORD because He has heard his voice and supplications as stated in Psalms 116:1.

questions.question: What does the psalmist plan to do as long as he lives?
questions.explanation: The psalmist states that he will call upon the LORD as long as he lives in Psalms 116:2.

questions.question: What encompassed the psalmist?
questions.explanation: The sorrows of death compassed the psalmist as mentioned in Psalms 116:3.

questions.question: What did the psalmist find?
questions.explanation: The psalmist found trouble and sorrow as stated in Psalms 116:3.

questions.question: What did the psalmist beseech the LORD for?
questions.explanation: The psalmist called upon the LORD, beseeching Him to deliver his soul as recorded in Psalms 116:4.

questions.question: How is the LORD described in Psalms 116?
questions.explanation: The LORD is described as gracious and righteous in Psalms 116:5.

questions.question: Who does the LORD preserve?
questions.explanation: The LORD preserveth the simple as stated in Psalms 116:6.

questions.question: What did the psalmist experience before he was helped?
options: He was in a state of joy
questions.explanation: The psalmist mentions that he was brought low before he received help from the LORD in Psalms 116:6.

questions.question: What should the psalmist's soul do?
questions.explanation: The psalmist instructs his soul to return unto its rest in Psalms 116:7.

questions.question: The LORD has dealt how with the psalmist?
questions.explanation: The LORD has dealt bountifully with the psalmist as stated in Psalms 116:7.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist loves the LORD.
questions.explanation: The psalmist states, 'I love the LORD' in Psalms 116:1.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD is described as merciful.
questions.explanation: The psalmist describes the LORD as merciful in Psalms 116:5.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist found joy and happiness.
questions.explanation: The psalmist found trouble and sorrow, not joy and happiness, as stated in Psalms 116:3.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist called upon the name of the LORD.
questions.explanation: The psalmist did call upon the name of the LORD, as stated in Psalms 116:4, not the opposite.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 116 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 116 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What has the LORD delivered my soul from according to Psalms 116:8?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD has delivered my soul from death, indicating the ultimate rescue from spiritual and physical death.

questions.question: What does Psalms 116:9 promise will happen if someone walks before the LORD?
options: They will live in the land of the living
questions.correctAnswer: They will live in the land of the living
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:9 states that the one who walks before the LORD will indeed be in the land of the living, emphasizing the connection between faithfulness and life.

questions.question: What does the psalmist express about his affliction in Psalms 116:10?
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly states that the psalmist believed and spoke about his great affliction, highlighting his honesty in prayer.

questions.question: What does the psalmist declare in his haste according to Psalms 116:11?
questions.explanation: In his haste, the psalmist declares that all men are liars, reflecting his moment of despair and distrust in humanity.

questions.question: What is the psalmist's question in Psalms 116:12 regarding God's benefits?
questions.explanation: The psalmist asks, 'What shall I render unto the LORD for all his benefits toward me?' indicating a desire to respond to God's goodness.

questions.question: What action does the psalmist promise to take in Psalms 116:13?
options: I will take the cup of salvation
I will call upon the people
questions.correctAnswer: I will take the cup of salvation
questions.explanation: The psalmist states that he will take the cup of salvation, symbolizing his acceptance of God's grace and mercy.

questions.question: What does the psalmist intend to do with his vows according to Psalms 116:14?
options: Pay them in the presence of all his people
questions.correctAnswer: Pay them in the presence of all his people
questions.explanation: The psalmist declares his intention to pay his vows to the LORD publicly, showing his commitment to God and accountability.

questions.question: How does Psalms 116:1 relate to the psalmist's actions in the following verses?
options: He loves the LORD because He has not answered
He loves the LORD because He has heard his voice
He loves the LORD because he is prosperous
He loves the LORD because he is free
questions.correctAnswer: He loves the LORD because He has heard his voice
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:1 indicates that the psalmist's love for the LORD is rooted in the experience of being heard in prayer, which motivates his response in later verses.

questions.question: What does Psalms 116:5 affirm about the character of the LORD?
questions.explanation: The psalmist describes the LORD as gracious and merciful, emphasizing the compassionate nature of God which underpins the psalmist's trust.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'Return unto thy rest, O my soul' in Psalms 116:7 suggest?
questions.explanation: This phrase indicates that the psalmist's soul can find peace and rest in the assurance that the LORD has dealt bountifully with him.

questions.question: How does Psalms 116:6 illustrate God's response to the psalmist's state?
questions.explanation: The verse states that God helped the psalmist when he was brought low, demonstrating God’s readiness to assist those in need.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 116:2, how long does the psalmist resolve to call upon the LORD?
questions.explanation: The psalmist expresses a commitment to call upon the LORD throughout his life, indicating a continual relationship with God.

questions.question: Is it true that the psalmist expresses doubt in humanity in Psalms 116:11?
questions.explanation: The psalmist's statement that 'All men are liars' reflects a moment of doubt and disillusionment with humanity.

questions.question: Is it false that the psalmist vows to pay his vows privately according to Psalms 116:14?
questions.explanation: The psalmist states he will pay his vows in the presence of all his people, which means he intends to do so publicly.

questions.question: Is it false that the psalmist believes he has no reason to call upon the LORD in Psalms 116:2?
questions.explanation: The psalmist affirms that he will call upon the LORD as long as he lives, indicating he has every reason to seek God.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 116 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 116.

questions.question: According to Psalms 116:15, whose death is described as 'precious in the sight of the LORD'?
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:15 explicitly states, 'Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of his saints.'

questions.question: In Psalms 116:16, how does the psalmist describe his relationship to the LORD?
options: Thy servant and the son of thine handmaid
questions.correctAnswer: Thy servant and the son of thine handmaid
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:16 says, 'O LORD, truly I am thy servant; I am thy servant, and the son of thine handmaid.'

questions.question: What does the psalmist vow to offer to the LORD according to Psalms 116:17?
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:17 declares, 'I will offer to thee the sacrifice of thanksgiving.'

questions.question: Where does the psalmist intend to pay his vows according to Psalms 116:18-19?
options: In the courts of the LORD's house, in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: In the courts of the LORD's house, in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:18-19 states, 'I will pay my vows unto the LORD now in the presence of all his people, in the courts of the LORD'S house, in the midst of thee, O Jerusalem.'

questions.question: What has the LORD done for the psalmist as mentioned in Psalms 116:16?
options: Wrote His law on my heart
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:16 includes the phrase, 'thou hast loosed my bonds,' indicating deliverance.

questions.question: Which phrase from Psalms 116:17 emphasizes continual reliance on God?
options: Will call upon the name of the LORD
Will build a temple for the LORD
Will sing alone in the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: Will call upon the name of the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:17 states, 'and will call upon the name of the LORD,' showing ongoing prayer and dependence.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'hesed' (חֶסֶד) found in Psalms 116:5 most accurately mean?
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:5 says, 'Gracious is the LORD,' where 'hesed' is understood as lovingkindness or steadfast love in Hebrew.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Psalms 116:15–19 to emphasize the psalmist's devotion?
questions.explanation: The passage begins and ends with praise and commitment to the LORD, framing the section as an inclusio (Psalms 116:15 and 116:19).

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of the preciousness of the death of the saints as in Psalms 116:15?
questions.explanation: Revelation 14:13 states, 'Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord...they rest from their labors,' echoing Psalms 116:15 about the preciousness of the saints' death.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects with the theme of deliverance and thanksgiving found in Psalms 116:4 and Psalms 116:17?
questions.explanation: Exodus 15:1 is the Song of Moses, a song of deliverance and praise, which parallels the thanksgiving and deliverance themes in Psalms 116:4 and 116:17.

questions.question: What verse immediately precedes Psalms 116:15, setting the stage for the reflection on the death of the saints?
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:14 precedes verse 15 and says, 'I will pay my vows unto the LORD now in the presence of all his people,' leading into the reflection on the preciousness of the saints' death.

questions.question: How does the psalmist describe God's character in Psalms 116:5 and how does this relate to the overall message of the chapter?
options: Gracious and righteous; it explains the reason for deliverance and thanksgiving
Jealous and angry; it warns against sin
Distant and unknowable; it emphasizes human struggle
Strict and unforgiving; it underscores judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Gracious and righteous; it explains the reason for deliverance and thanksgiving
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:5 states, 'Gracious is the LORD, and righteous; yea, our God is merciful,' which undergirds the psalmist's reason for thanksgiving and deliverance.

questions.question: What typology can be seen in Psalms 116:13 'I will take the cup of salvation' when compared to New Testament symbolism?
options: The cup as a symbol of Christ's sacrifice in the Lord's Supper
The cup as a symbol of judgment in Revelation
The cup representing the water of life in John
The cup as a symbol of the manna in the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: The cup as a symbol of Christ's sacrifice in the Lord's Supper
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:13's 'cup of salvation' prefigures the New Testament Lord's Supper cup symbolizing Christ's sacrificial blood (cf. Luke 22:20).

questions.question: What parallelism is found in Psalms 116:8 that emphasizes deliverance?
options: Deliver my soul from death, mine eyes from tears, and my feet from falling
The mountains skipped like rams, and the little hills like lambs
He makes me lie down in green pastures and leads me beside still waters
The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want
questions.correctAnswer: Deliver my soul from death, mine eyes from tears, and my feet from falling
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:8 uses synonymous parallelism listing deliverance in three areas: soul, eyes, and feet, emphasizing comprehensive rescue.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 116:19 ends with a call to praise the LORD in the midst of Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:19 concludes, 'Praise ye the LORD,' in the midst of Jerusalem, affirming the call to worship.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 116 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 116 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 116:5 teach about God's nature?
options: God is indifferent to human suffering
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:5 states, 'Gracious is the LORD, and righteous; yea, our God is merciful,' affirming God's graciousness, righteousness, and mercy as essential aspects of His nature.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding human affliction and faith is taught in Psalms 116:10?
options: Affliction proves the absence of faith
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:10 says, 'I believed, therefore have I spoken: I was greatly afflicted,' indicating that true faith does not preclude suffering but endures through it.

questions.question: What doctrine about salvation is taught in Psalms 116:13?
options: Salvation is embraced by calling upon the Lord
Salvation is a future event only
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is embraced by calling upon the Lord
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:13 states, 'I will take the cup of salvation, and call upon the name of the LORD,' teaching that salvation involves calling on God’s name in faith and gratitude.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 116:6 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:6 says, 'The LORD preserveth the simple: I was brought low, and he helped me,' demonstrating God's attribute of preservation and care for the vulnerable.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Psalms 116:15?
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:15 states, 'Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of his saints,' emphasizing God's valuing and honoring of His saints, reflecting His holiness and covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: How does Psalms 116:1–2 connect to the New Testament teaching on prayer and persistent faith?
options: It prefigures the call to continual prayer as seen in 1 Thessalonians 5:17
It contradicts the doctrine of prayer being necessary
It teaches prayer is optional for believers
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the call to continual prayer as seen in 1 Thessalonians 5:17
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:1–2 shows the psalmist's commitment to call upon the Lord as long as he lives, which aligns with the New Testament exhortation to 'pray without ceasing' (1 Thessalonians 5:17).

questions.question: How does Psalms 116:8 prepare for the theme of deliverance in the Gospel?
options: By illustrating deliverance from death and despair by God’s intervention
By denying any deliverance is possible
By emphasizing human effort over divine help
By focusing only on physical healing
questions.correctAnswer: By illustrating deliverance from death and despair by God’s intervention
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:8 says, 'For thou hast delivered my soul from death, mine eyes from tears, and my feet from falling,' foreshadowing the deliverance through Christ from spiritual death and sorrow.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 116:12 and 116:14 teach about worship and vow-keeping?
options: Gratitude expressed through public vow fulfillment honors God
Vows are private and need not be fulfilled
Worship is only inward and needs no outward expression
Vows are optional and not important
questions.correctAnswer: Gratitude expressed through public vow fulfillment honors God
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:12 asks what to render to the LORD for his benefits, and 116:14 commits to paying vows in the presence of all his people, teaching that worship includes public and faithful vow-keeping as an expression of gratitude.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 116:16 and 116:17 teach about servanthood and thanksgiving?
options: True servanthood involves offering thanksgiving sacrifices and calling on the Lord
Servanthood is only about obedience without worship
questions.correctAnswer: True servanthood involves offering thanksgiving sacrifices and calling on the Lord
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:16 confesses servanthood to God who has loosed the bonds, and 116:17 promises thanksgiving sacrifices and calling upon the Lord, teaching thanksgiving as integral to faithful servanthood.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 116:3 and 116:11 teach about human despair and the limits of human speech?
options: Human despair can lead to distrust and false generalizations about mankind
Human speech always reflects divine truth
Human speech is infallible in crisis
questions.correctAnswer: Human despair can lead to distrust and false generalizations about mankind
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:3 describes being surrounded by sorrows and death, and 116:11 states, 'All men are liars,' spoken in haste, showing how despair can distort perception and speech.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Psalms 116:15 implies God values the death of saints more than their lives. What does Psalms 116:15 actually teach?
options: The death of saints is precious to God because it signifies their faithful completion
God prefers the death of saints over their service
God is indifferent to the death of saints
The verse teaches that saints’ lives are cheap to God
questions.correctAnswer: The death of saints is precious to God because it signifies their faithful completion
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:15 states, 'Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of his saints,' meaning God honors the faithful completion of their pilgrimage, not that He prefers death over life.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's merciful listening is taught in Psalms 116:1?
options: God hears and responds to the supplications of His people
God is silent and unresponsive to prayers
God only listens to the righteous
God’s hearing is limited by human worthiness
questions.correctAnswer: God hears and responds to the supplications of His people
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:1 says, 'I love the LORD, because he hath heard my voice and my supplications,' teaching that God's mercy includes actively hearing and responding to prayers.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is especially demonstrated in Psalms 116:7?
options: God’s bountifulness and provision of rest
questions.correctAnswer: God’s bountifulness and provision of rest
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:7 says, 'Return unto thy rest, O my soul; for the LORD hath dealt bountifully with thee,' highlighting God's generous provision and care.

questions.question: What theological theme is highlighted by the repeated vow fulfillment mentioned in Psalms 116:14 and 116:18?
options: The importance of covenant faithfulness and public witness in worship
The irrelevance of vows in true faith
The superiority of private devotion over public worship
questions.correctAnswer: The importance of covenant faithfulness and public witness in worship
questions.explanation: Both verses emphasize paying vows in the presence of all God’s people, teaching the theological importance of covenant fidelity and public worship as testimony.

questions.question: How does Psalms 116:9 relate to sanctification in the life of the believer?
options: Walking before the LORD in the land of the living demonstrates ongoing sanctification
Sanctification is irrelevant to daily living
Believers are sanctified instantly and need not walk with God
Sanctification is only future, not present
questions.correctAnswer: Walking before the LORD in the land of the living demonstrates ongoing sanctification
questions.explanation: Psalms 116:9 states, 'I will walk before the LORD in the land of the living,' teaching the doctrine that sanctification involves a continual, faithful walk with God in life.
